$comment: Per-subpath gzip budgets (budget model v3). Keys are export subpaths without './'. Every chart needs an entry — gen-size-limits.mjs fails on a missing one, so adding a chart forces a budget decision. `.size-limit.json` is GENERATED from this file + package.json#exports — never hand-edit it. THE CONTRACT, in the order CI applies it: (1) every subpath is gated by its own measured budget below, set to measured + max(50 B, 2%); (2) every PR is diffed against its base branch and growth over 1% on any subpath fails; (3) a NEW chart is admitted at static ≤ 3 kB and interactive ≤ static + 3.25 kB; (4) nothing, shipped or new, exceeds the catalog ceiling of static 4.35 kB / interactive 7 kB — the interactive wall is HARD and no sign-off raises it. Rules 3 and 4 are stated in full under $ceilings.
$exception: Sparkline 3.35/4.35 kB was USER-APPROVED (2026-07-08) as a flagship exception to the 3/4 kB hard caps (long-series guard + label=minmax; trims exhausted first). Batch 1 W4 raised it to 3.65/4.65 kB PENDING user sign-off at the batch gate: the annotations HOST contract adds the children walker + scale frame (~0.29 kB) to every S1/S2 host — the annotation MARK renderers ship in ./annotations (1.46 kB), which consumers import separately, so hosts only pay the walker. Not a precedent for other charts. ANNOTATION-HOST RETROFIT (2026-07-15, USER-APPROVED full value-series family): resolveAnnotations walker + scale frame added to 15 value-series hosts. 5 cross the 3 kB static ceiling as approved exceptions (all < Sparkline 3.65): change-point 3.45, win-prob-worm 3.4, forecast-cone/dual-sparkline 3.35, burn-chart 3.25. The other 10 stay < 3 kB.
$interaction: INTERACTION-CONTRACT RE-BASELINE (2026-07-18, USER-APPROVED): the shared useActivePicker kernel (shared/interactive.ts) adds the standardized onActive/onSelect callbacks + controlled selection (selectedIndex/defaultSelectedIndex) + touch tap-select to every MULTI-UNIT interactive entry. Because size-limit bundles shared code standalone per subpath, the kernel costs ~0.49–0.53 kB gzip on each such interactive entry (static entries unchanged). Multi-unit interactive budgets are raised by ~0.5 kB to absorb it; pure-scalar charts (delta, status-dot, trend-arrow, moon-phase, thermometer, progress, progress-ring, fat-digits, dice-pips, tally-marks, hourglass, breathing-dot, eta-bar, heartbeat-blip, fill-word, tape-gauge) keep the lean whole-chart onSelect and stay at their current budgets.
$seat: INLINE-SEAT RE-BASELINE (2026-07-19, USER-APPROVED). Every chart now emits a `Seat` (mode + plot box) from its geometry so `.mc-inline` can sit the mark on the text line — see `Seat` in src/shared/Chart.tsx. Measured cost by controlled experiment (removed one chart's seat, rebuilt): 25 B gzip per subpath. All 211 chart budgets were re-measured from the built dist and rewritten to the next 10 B above actual. CAVEAT, recorded deliberately: this re-baseline could NOT isolate the seat from the concurrent interaction-contract migration, which was still mid-flight in the same working tree — total drift absorbed was 13,002 B across 183 subpaths (median 70 B), of which only ~25 B/subpath is attributable to the seat. Re-verify these numbers once the interaction-contract migration finishes. NEW 3 kB STATIC EXCEPTIONS (11, beyond the 6 already listed in $exception): station-glyph 3.28, slope 3.25, spread-band 3.21, control-strip 3.13, retention-curve 3.13, percentile-ladder 3.10, queue-depth 3.09, shift-histogram 3.08, sparkbar 3.08, polar-clock 3.06, stacked-area 3.05. Each is < 0.3 kB over the ceiling and none is a precedent for a new chart, which still must land under 3 kB.
$ceilings: CEILING DECISION (resolved 2026-08-03; replaces the STALE-RULE NOTE of 2026-07-26). Two rules in CLAUDE.md had stopped describing the shipped catalog and neither was enforced per entry. Both are now settled, and the numbers below are measured from a fresh build of 217 subpaths. RETIRED: `interactive ≤ static + 1 kB`. It was never reachable. size-limit bundles each subpath standalone, so every interactive entry is charged the whole shared picker/announce/seat kernel — kernel:interactive minus kernel:static in size-snapshot.mjs, ~1.8 kB of chunk source, ~2.4 kB once bundled per entry. Measured deltas across the 106 pairs run 1.01–3.12 kB, median 2.45 kB, so all 106 broke the old rule and none of them broke anything real. The replacement admission bar is `interactive ≤ static + 3.25 kB`: the kernel plus ~0.85 kB of entry code. The whole catalog meets it, and it still fails an entry that re-implements shared work locally instead of composing the static and the picker. REFRAMED: `static ≤ 3 kB` is an ADMISSION bar for a new chart, not a catalog ceiling. 32 shipped statics measure 3.02–4.25 kB. Each one's size is the recorded cost of a named feature — the annotations host walker, direct-label gutter math, derived statistics, a second series or band, a second orientation — itemized in the $ notes below. A byte review on 2026-08-03 looked for slack and found none: the shared kernel tree-shakes correctly (micro-donut measures 2985 B and does not carry segmented-bar's 2684 B), dev warnings are not eliminable because their messages are call arguments (esbuild with `process.env.NODE_ENV` defined to production measures the same 2752 B on ohlc either way), and the largest entries are dense feature code rather than duplication. They stay, governed by rules (1) and (2) in $comment. 74 chart statics remain under 3 kB, so the bar that put them there is unchanged and these 32 are not a precedent. CATALOG CEILING: static 4.35 kB / interactive 7 kB. USER-SET 2026-08-03: 7 kB is a HARD wall on any interactive subpath, not crossable by sign-off. It is the number the README, the docs and the package description all quote (“~2–7 kB interactive”), so crossing it would make published copy false. Sparkline defines the top of both scales (4245 / 6995 measured) and its interactive budget is pinned AT the wall — 7000 B, 5 B of headroom — rather than at measured + 2%, which would have sat 135 B over it. Any growth on that subpath fails the size gate, by design; buy room by shrinking the entry, never by raising this number. Static 4.35 kB keeps its normal sign-off route.
$polish: CHART-POLISH PASS (2026-07-21): P0/P1 labelFont/fontWeight/motion-safety + sibling API parity (annotations hosts, optional labels, glyph pop entrances). Measured cost after one-pass gutter math on ensemble/net-flow/forecast-cone and gated label work: ensemble-ghosts +0.74 kB static (annotations walker + end label), bullet/micro-donut/honeycomb optional labels +0.24–0.35 kB even at default none (feature ships in the entry), annotation hosts ~+0.21–0.29 kB each, glyph useEntrance ~+0.22–0.31 kB interactive. Budgets re-measured with max(50 B, 2%) headroom. NEW charts still held to 3 kB / +1 kB.
$hover: HOVER-INDEX CORRECTNESS (2026-07-19): four charts emitted or consumed the wrong index space on hover — ohlc read a filtered position back against the unfiltered periods, retention-curve emitted a period but consumed a position, pareto-strip/percentile-ladder made unpainted marks navigable, polar-clock inverted a raw `start`. The fixes carry a source index through geometry and switch the sparse spaces to `navOrder`, costing: ohlc 2.64→2.65 / 4.61→4.73, retention-curve interactive 5.14→5.24, pareto-strip 2.45→2.49 / 4.51→4.62, polar-clock 3.07→3.09 / 5.12→5.15. percentile-ladder was unchanged. polar-clock's static exception listed in $seat moves 3.06→3.09; it stays under the other approved statics and is not a precedent.
$dismiss: LIGHT-DISMISS RE-BASELINE (2026-08-06). The shared picker kernel (src/shared/interactive.ts) now binds `pointerdown` + `keydown` on the window WHILE a unit is pinned, so a press outside the chart — or Escape from anywhere — drops the selection; a pin used to be reachable only by re-selecting the same unit or by pressing Escape on a chart that still had focus. Measured on a fresh build: kernel:interactive 4144 -> 4198 B, and +~50 B gzip on each of the ~85 multi-unit interactive subpaths. 14 of them crossed their budget by 1-44 B and are re-based here at measured + max(50 B, 2%); the other ~71 absorbed it inside the headroom they already had. Statics are untouched — the kernel is client-only. SPARKLINE PAID FOR ITSELF: ./sparkline/interactive is pinned AT the 7 kB wall, which no sign-off raises, so the room came out of the entry instead. In the kernel: the wrap() default cache is a plain object with `??=` rather than a Map, `datum` is required (all 84 picker charts pass one, so the index-only fallback was dead weight), navOrder indexes its order array directly, the pointerdown stamp shares the `down` ref the tap/drag test already kept, and the listeners bind through the bare `addEventListener` globals. In the chart: uiGroup() is inlined into its only caller, the two UI marks are destructured once, and the readout gates on the geometry point rather than re-testing the value (which also stopped a pin that outlived its series, or one aimed at a gap, from announcing 'Point 0 of 3: NaN'). Net 6970 -> 6991 B, inside the wall by 9 B. NOT a precedent for spending the remaining margin: the next change to that entry has to find its own bytes.
$labelsize: LABEL-SIZE PIN (2026-07-19): `styles.css` sets `font-size` on `.mc-root text`, and a CSS declaration outranks an SVG presentation attribute, so a chart's `fontSize={n}` was inert unless it also pinned `--mc-label-size`. 22 charts did not, and painted labels at 1.3-2.4x the size their gutters were computed for — measured spills up to 17.5 viewBox units past the viewBox, at default size, with the catalog's own sample data (src/test/label-containment.browser.test.tsx reproduces it). Pinning the var costs ~30 B gzip per affected subpath (+1.35 kB across the catalog). Twelve budgets are raised here to absorb it, each to ~60 B of headroom. Sparkline static 3.7 -> 3.8 kB touches the USER-APPROVED flagship exception above and needs the same sign-off. The alternative to paying these bytes is shipping charts whose labels paint into the page, so the bytes are not optional. STREAK-SPARK LABEL BAND (same pass): its geometry reserved no room above the runs, so the DEFAULT label="current" rendered nothing below ~48 units against a default height of 20 — a documented prop that did nothing at word size. Reserving the band costs ~50 B static / ~20 B interactive; both budgets raised here.
$readout: READOUT-PARITY RE-BASELINE (2026-07-26, USER-APPROVED): every interactive entry now PAINTS the reading it already announced. Three pickers (comet-trail, icon-array, pictogram-row) shipped a hover ring + live-region announcement and no chip at all; nine scalars (progress, progress-ring, hourglass, breathing-dot, heartbeat-blip, fill-word, tape-gauge, minimap-strip, token-confidence) hid their number whenever the static label was off or dropped. Cost is the chip JSX plus, on the scalars, a hover/focus state pair: +20 B (comet-trail) to +220 B (token-confidence, which must MEASURE its token to place the chip over flowing text). Budgets re-measured from the built dist with ~2% headroom. Guarded by src/test/readout-presence.test.ts, so a new chart cannot ship interaction without a readout. P0 FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-26): bullet +50 B (it was the one interactive entry with no announcement channel — a LiveRegion, which also replaces its hand-rolled useSeatHoist), calendar-strip static +60 B (dev-only SSR warning for the clock-reading `end` default), token-confidence +70 B (delegated focus/hover handlers + the decorative opt-out). REVIEW FOLLOW-UP: eta-bar interactive 3.62→3.63 kB — the staged budget sat 2 B BELOW the built entry (the hover-reveal rewrite landed after that measurement), so `pnpm size` was red on the branch before this bump; heat-cell and icon-array picked up new `strings` tokens (levelChip, iconArrayRatio) inside their existing headroom.
$robust: RENDER-ROBUSTNESS RE-BASELINE (2026-07-20, tests/craft/robust.mjs): balance-beam, fat-digits, forecast-cone and tape-gauge crashed or leaked NaN/undefined into markup and into aria-labels on degenerate input (empty/short pair, null pan, non-finite domain, short interval pair, malformed zone). The fixes validate each number where it ENTERS geometry (isFiniteValue guards on the pan values, the tier domain, the p80/p50 bounds and the zone bounds), degrade the summaries to the shared `noData` wording, and give TapeGauge a visible no-reading rail so an empty gauge cannot read as a reading of zero. Cost: +4 B (fat-digits) to +134 B (balance-beam) static. NOTE: ~95 B of each INTERACTIVE bump here is pre-existing tree-wide drift shared by all 105 interactive entries (see $ceilings), not this change. FINAL 7 (2026-07-20, same harness, suite now 0): calibration-strip leaked <rect y="NaN"> from an ∞/∞ support-lane scale, minimap-strip THREW in makeFormatter on a short/null `window` (and leaked NaN from a non-finite one), spread-band put `undefined` in an aria-label from a series-label pair shorter than two. Same discipline: guard where the number enters geometry, resolve the pair once, fall back to each chart's existing `noData` string, and give MinimapStrip a hollow dashed rail when the window is unmeasurable (empty ≠ a window at zero). Cost, static: calibration-strip 2.58→2.59, spread-band 3.22→3.25 (still inside the $seat exception list), minimap-strip 2.52→2.70 — the largest, being a window resolver + known-extent filter + `domain`-prop validator. Interactive budgets here add ONLY each chart's own delta; the residual ~95 B is the same tree-wide drift noted above.
$readoutvalue: READOUT VALUE-VISIBILITY PASS (2026-07-26): a readout may not drop a number the caller passed in. Chips and announcements now carry the magnitude behind every derived share (confusion-grid the cell tally, partition-strip/likert-strip/volume-profile the value behind the share, segmented-bar/micro-donut the rolled-up Other total), StackedArea names every band instead of the leading one, ActivityGrid names the day when `anchor` dates the grid, and a measured zero stopped rendering as "no data" (seismogram) while an empty bucket stopped rendering as zero (waveform). Where a richer chip would have ellipsized at the chart's own width, it became ROWS (`.mc-readout-rows`, one row per member, name column capped at 7em) rather than a longer line — readout-containment.browser.test.tsx still gates verbosity, and readout-value-visibility.browser.test.tsx now gates the other direction. Only 3 subpaths moved past their budget, all interactive: activity-grid 5.17→5.42 (UTC day math + date formatter), stacked-area 5.91→6.05 (row chip), partition-strip 4.85→5.17 (row chip + value formatter + the new format/locale props). Statics unchanged; measured + max(50 B, 2%) per $rebaseline.
$rebaseline: SIZE RE-BASELINE (2026-07-20, scripts/rebaseline-sizes.mjs): every budget reset to measured + max(50 B, 2%) headroom after the release hardening pass (fillFor sizing fix ~90 B/interactive entry, per-chart degradation label-drop gates ~42–119 B/static, null/NaN geometry guards). 149 budgets raised, 65 tightened — subpaths that shrank were pulled DOWN to lock the win in, which the old ~10 B-above-actual policy would have missed. The 2% band absorbs shared-kernel byte churn instead of firing all 106 interactive entries on a one-line helper edit.
$systemic: SYSTEMIC-AUDIT RE-BASELINE (2026-07-26): 44 budgets raised to measured + max(50 B, 2%) per $rebaseline. Only the entries that went over are touched — a full re-baseline would tighten ~170 others in the same commit and bury the deltas that need reading. Four causes, all of them things the library already claimed and nothing checked. (1) `onActive` on the 19 NON-PICKER scalars (+2 B pictogram-row to +91 B delta): the shared interaction contract and the quickstart both documented `onActive` as universal while those entries implemented `onSelect` alone, so the `readout={false}` + `datum.formatted` KPI pattern worked on 84 charts and not on 19. Cost is one datum builder shared by both callbacks plus an edge-gate ref, because pointer-enter and focus both mean 'active' and would otherwise fire twice. (2) The percent-formatter sweep (+3 B micro-donut static to +280 B fill-word interactive): every hardcoded `${n}%` now goes through one `makePercentFormatter`, and the five charts that had no `locale` to thread gained one. The biggest movers are the charts where the percent is the ONLY number and there was no formatter to share — fill-word, moon-phase, hourglass, time-in-range, pareto-strip pay for the Intl plumbing on a ~1.5-2.5 kB base, which is why a 200 B delta reads as 12-18% there and under 2% on a figure-scale chart. (3) `annotations` +39 B: the label layer sets `--mc-label-size` (its `fontSize` attribute was inert), seats labels on a clamped central baseline, and runs Marker's label through the truncator every other annotation already used. (4) `theme` +41 B: `defineTheme` derives `--mc-on-cat` from its own generated palette, so the measured 4.5:1 label contrast travels with a custom accent instead of being silently voided by one. The rest (calendar-strip, heartbeat-blip, orbit-status, sprout-row, waveform, win-prob-worm, bias-strip, change-point) is per-chart work plus the shared-kernel byte churn the 2% band exists to absorb. No NEW chart is admitted under these numbers: the 3 kB / +1 kB ceiling still applies to one.
$windbarb: WIND-BARB INTERACTIVE ENTRY (2026-08-02, completeness pass): the chart shipped static-only; the interactive entry (live announce + pop entrance + whole-chart onActive/onSelect, the pure-scalar shape from $interaction) was added with its browser tests. The budget staged at 4.18 kB sat BELOW the built entry (4224 B), so `pnpm size` was red on this tree — the same failure mode eta-bar hit in $readout. Re-measured to 4.31 kB per the measured + max(50 B, 2%) rule.
$fieldreport: FIELD-REPORT RE-BASELINE (2026-08-07). Four changes landed together, all of them sweeps rather than point fixes, so this re-baselines every budget to measured + max(50 B, 2%) per $rebaseline. (1) makeFormatter split: `format` now MERGES with a chart's own defaults instead of replacing them (`format={{notation:"compact"}}` on a percent chart rendered 3% as 0.03), and the merging path moved to a separate `makeUnitFormatter` so the ~75 charts that format a bare number are not charged for a branch they cannot reach — measured 95 B gzip per subpath, which is the difference between ./sparkline/interactive sitting under the wall and over it. Cost lands only on the 27 charts with formatting defaults (funnel +55, honeycomb +52, delta +115). (2) labelSize: every chart that paints an in-SVG label takes a `labelSize` prop that raises labelFont's 7-unit floor through GEOMETRY, because that is where the gutter is reserved; charts now pin their computed size as `--mc-label-px` so the app-facing `--mc-label-size` stops being clobbered on exactly the charts that paint labels. (3) Sub-unit marks: a stylesheet rule relaxes `crispEdges` below 1 unit, where the hint snapped a 0.5-unit visibility floor to zero device pixels and a bin holding 4 events painted what a bin holding 0 painted. Net -6 B of JS across the catalog; the cost is 25 B on styles.css. (4) sparkbar containment: y and height were rounded independently, so each could round up 0.005 and the pair summed past the viewBox (found by the property test, red on main). SPARKLINE IS CLAMPED AT THE CEILING, NOT AT measured + 2%: interactive 7.00 kB (measured 6985, 15 B of room) and static 4.35 kB (measured 4255). The 7 kB wall is USER-SET and quoted in the README, the docs and the package description; no sign-off raises it. The `labelSize` prop was fitted inside that margin rather than paid for by raising the number. A per-chart dev warning for oversized width/height was DESIGNED AND DROPPED for the same reason: measured +86 B on ./sparkline/interactive (7079) and +100 B static (4355), past both ceilings. The authored maximums ship as catalog metadata instead, which costs nothing and is what an agent reads anyway.
$scalarkernel: SCALAR-KERNEL RE-BASELINE (2026-08-11). Two sweeps landed together and re-chunked the shared kernel, so every budget is reset to measured + max(50 B, 2%) per $rebaseline. (1) The 20 single-unit (scalar) clients moved onto one shared useScalarActive hook (src/shared/interactive.ts): the verbatim activate() blocks and six inline listeners each carried are gone, Escape now lowers the reveal on every scalar, and the five chip-less scalars memo their static SVG so a hover edge stays render-free. Cost: +31 B (heat-cell) to +81 B (fat-digits) per scalar interactive entry. (2) The four charts that hand-rolled aria-live spans render the shared LiveRegion, which made interactive.ts + live-region.tsx + seat-hoist.ts share one importer set — rollup now emits them as a single chunk, and ~90 multi-unit interactive entries shrank 9-23 B each from the deduped module overhead (./sparkline/interactive 6985 -> 6973, gaining headroom against the 7 kB wall it is pinned at). minimap-strip concentrates the merge cost (+223 B): its bespoke slider never calls the picker kernel, but the merged chunk carries it past what a re-bundle can tree-shake — accepted, at 4581 B it sits mid-pack. resolveSummary adoption in 36 statics moved stats.ts into the summary chunk (statics +7-17 B where the two halves used to split); KERNELS in size-snapshot.mjs now declares the merged chunks. Kernel readings: static 2458 -> 2446, interactive 4306 -> 4405.
